entities.summary:
Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah Al-Azraqi was a 9th-century Islamic commentator and historian who authored the Book of Reports about Mecca. Born in the Arabian Peninsula, Al-Azraqi was influenced by the early Islamic scholarly tradition and developed a distinctive approach to historical writing. His work, which covered the history of the Meccan region from the pre-Islamic period to the 8th century CE, was widely used by later Islamic historians and remains an important source for understanding the early history of Islam.

This significance can be seen in the fact that Al-Azraqi's work was widely used by later Islamic historians such as Al-Tabari and Al-Masudi, who drew heavily on his research. Furthermore, Al-Azraqi's focus on the history of the Meccan region helped to establish the region as a major center of Islamic learning and culture.

In terms of its legacy, Al-Azraqi's work has had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic historiography. His approach to historical writing, which emphasized the importance of primary sources and detailed descriptions of events, helped to shape the field of Islamic historiography for centuries to come.

One notable example of Al-Azraqi's influence can be seen in the work of the 19th-century Ottoman historian, Mustafa Nami.

Al-Azraqi's work also had a significant impact on the development of modern historiography. His emphasis on the importance of primary sources and detailed descriptions of events helped to establish the field of historiography as we know it today.
